# Mobile Cleanliness — Phase Three: Tiferes Execution Order

The Awtsmoos binds beauty to boundary so no light spills uselessly past the vessel;
Awtsmoos.com will look advanced because every edge, state, and transition is deliberate and restful.

## Final execution order

### Wave A — Newly exposed surfaces
1. Adventure: inspect entry HTML, loaded CSS, menu/HUD controls, canvas/game sizing, and touch controls. Verify 390×844 and 320×568 with any menus opened.
2. Ohrbound: inspect HUD, pause/settings surfaces, touch controls, overlays, viewport assumptions, and orientation behavior.
3. DB Console: inspect forms, query/result tables, control rows, modal/menu behavior, and mobile stacking. Prioritize the known form-width/mobile risk only if reproduced.
4. Broadcaster: inspect studio panes, device controls, previews, transport buttons, sidebars, and responsive shell.

### Wave B — Previously modified flagship surfaces
5. Video Editor: run isolated mobile/desktop acceptance of drawers, timeline, transport, popovers, focus, and pointer/touch controls. Change source only if acceptance exposes a real regression.

### Wave C — Global hygiene
6. Static scan all public app/game CSS and HTML for risky fixed/min widths, `100vw`, four-digit z-indexes, fixed-position menus without viewport constraints, unmatched hover/active states, and selectors with conflicting mobile geometry.
7. Readiness-aware browser sampling across risk-ranked routes. Discard pre-CSS measurements and wait for route-specific app readiness or stable stylesheet/resource conditions.
8. Fix only confirmed defects, smallest coherent surface first, while rewriting every touched file completely and splitting any oversized responsibility.

## Production design contract

- No document horizontal overflow from interface chrome.
- No visible menu, popover, dialog, or drawer extends beyond phone edges when open.
- Fixed/sticky primary actions respect safe areas and never cover unrelated controls.
- Every action control has hover + active + focus-visible states where applicable.
- Touch targets are practically reachable; decorative tiny controls are not mistaken for actions.
- Advanced controls are collapsed/retractable on mobile when they are not necessary for the default task.
- Menus use `max-inline-size`, viewport-aware positioning, internal scrolling, and safe padding rather than relying on page overflow.
- Tables/code/results use contained horizontal scrolling rather than expanding the document.
- Any visual animation must be short, stateful, interruptible, and disabled/reduced under `prefers-reduced-motion` when nonessential.
- No page may end in raw browser-default fields, orphan buttons, unfinished placeholder cards, or styling that abruptly stops midway through the DOM.

## Verification after every rewrite

Read every touched file fully. Run syntax/line/indentation/long-line gates. Re-run the exact failing viewport/state. Then test a second narrower viewport and short height. Finally compare planned defects to actual changes and create a delta before moving to the next route.
